guides.source_note: Rules of thumb used in residential furniture planning: about 24 in is a tight single-file squeeze, 30 in is comfortable, 36 in is generous and the usual allowance in front of a dresser for opening drawers and standing. For reference, 36 in is also the US International Residential Code minimum hallway width (IRC R311.6). These are guides, not code requirements for bedrooms.
guides.note_shallowest_miles_dresser: Every Miles dresser in West Elm's US line is 18 in deep or more (60, 70: 18; 34: 18.3; 48 narrow and 49 wide: 19.3), so no Miles dresser on the west wall widens the aisle.

shaker_door_stop_requested.model: Leaf pivots at the hinge edge (pin x 0.5); stop = first contact with the dresser. Margin m = hinge edge y - dresser south end y. m >= 0: 90 + atan(m/18.25) deg (the dresser's front corner stops the leaf just past a right angle). m < 0: atan(0.25/|m|) deg (the dresser end sits in front of the hinge and blocks the door early).
shaker_door_stop_requested.plain: Both estimates say the white door opens to about a right angle and rests against the dresser end (about 93 deg survey, 90.5 deg photo fit), but the margin is thin: the dresser's end would stop only 0.15 to 1 inch short of the door's hinge edge. If it ends up past the hinge edge even half an inch (for example if the north window sill sticks out more than 2 inches), the door would be blocked early, at roughly 15 to 30 degrees.

shaker_door_stop_alternative.note: Zero-thickness front-corner estimate; the round-3 build's leaf model gave 122.0 at the survey hinge. Opens well past a right angle across the whole range; exact value is not decision-relevant.

measurements_requested: On the west wall above the baseboard, measure from the north wall to the hinge edge of the white door, where the door meets its frame on the hinge side (estimates 62.15 to 63 in). Also measure how far the north window's sill (stool) sticks out from the wall (estimate 2 in). If the hinge edge is at least 60 inches plus the sill projection from the north wall, the 60-inch dresser stops short of it and becomes the door's stop at about a right angle; if not, the dresser sits in front of the hinge and blocks the door early.

From the north wall to the outer north edge of the white door's trim (estimates 58.3 to 59.5 in), and how far that trim stands out from the wall compared with the baseboard (if it stands out more, the dresser must sit out from the wall by the difference, narrowing the walkway).

On the east wall: from the north wall to where the east window's sill and trim begin (estimate 81 in), how far that sill sticks out (estimate 2 in), and its height from the floor (estimate 28 to 30 in). The queen's 45-inch headboard reaches 90.6 in from the north wall, so it overlaps that window.
Clear room width from the west wall to the east wall at about 30 inches high, plus baseboard thickness.
White door width, and how far it opens today before hitting anything.
